universal_lens: Pose estimation and tracking via heatmaps, bounding boxes, and feature-based association form a unified pipeline for player identification. A unified framework for multi-object tracking integrates geometric, visual, and deep learning features via MOTA optimization under stabilized and non-stabilized video sequences.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference on player tracks uses probabilistic feature matching to update belief states over time. Bayesian inference models track objects using feature vector posteriors, with conformal prediction bounds on MOTA accuracy for real-time decision-making in dynamic sports environments.
gse_mapping: Situationally aware state transitions model player movement and court interactions through geometric and visual feature dynamics. Situationally-aware state transitions in GSE map object identities across frames using pose-based feature fusion, enabling predictive tracking under uncertainty and temporal instability.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter four presents a methodological framework for multi-object tracking in basketball videos using a combination of geometric, visual, and deep learning features. The core innovation lies in optimizing Multiple Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA) through systematic ablation studies. The paper evaluates how different feature types—geometric shape descriptors, color similarity measures, and deep learning embeddings from VGG-19—contribute independently and collectively to tracking performance. It demonstrates that while combining all features yields a slight improvement in MOTA, the added computational complexity makes pure deep learning features more practical. The analysis also explores the impact of neighborhood size and stabilization parameters on tracking consistency. A key finding is that specific body parts like shoulders, chest, and hips provide strong discriminative power, whereas extremities such as elbows and ankles contribute less. This suggests that tracking algorithms should prioritize high-contrast, structurally stable regions of the human form. The work establishes a baseline for future research in real-time sports analytics by quantifying trade-offs between accuracy and efficiency.
